newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS GET MATT WILLIAMS FROM GIANTS FOR THREE PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS GET MATT WILLIAMS FROM GIANTS FOR THREE PLAYERS.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians, facing the possible free-agent defection of slugger Albert Belle, acquired star third baseman Matt Williams from the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday for three players.
The Giants received reliever Julian Tavarez and infielders Jose Vizcaino and Jeff Kent in the deal. Each team also included a player to be named later and Cleveland may add cash to complete the deal.

Williams was limited to 105 games by a shoulder injury in 1996, but still hit .302 with 22 homers and 85 runs batted in. His powerful bat could fill a void created by the potential departure of Belle, who rejected the Indians' offer of a reported $41 million over five years on Tuesday.
Despite winning more games over the last two years than any other team, the Indians again showed they are not afraid to re-tool their roster.
Kent and Vizcaino were acquired during the season from the New York Mets for All-Star Carlos Baerga and first baseman Eddie Murray was traded to the Baltimore Orioles.

"Matt Williams is arguably the best all-around third baseman in the game today," Indians executive vice president John Hart said. "Matt Williams is a special player in that he can hit for average and power and is an excellent fielding third baseman. He is a tremendous addition to our ballclub."

"It was an incredibly difficult decision to trade Matt Williams, one of the game's finest players and competitors," Giants senior vice president Brian Sabean said from the general managers' meetings in Phoenix.
"As hard of a decision as it was, all things considered, this deal makes the Giants a better team. It is just the beginning of our plans to turn the organisation around."

Williams, who turns 31 later this month, is signed through 1998 at more than $6 million per season. In addition to his bat, Williams has won three Gold Gloves for his fielding. To make room for him, Cleveland would move third baseman Jim Thome -- another slugger -- across the diamond to first base.

However, Williams has been injury-prone. After a career-high 43 homers in the strike-shortened 1994 campaign, he missed nearly half the 1995 season with a broken foot. The four-time All-Star hasn't played more than 150 games in a season since 1991.

Tavarez, 23, addresses the Giants' need for pitching. After going 10-2 with a 2.44 earned run average in 1995, he slumped to 4-7 and 5.36 last season. But he throws very hard and has a live arm, enabling him to start or relieve. He also is signed through 1998, with club options for 1999 and 2000.

Vizcaino and Kent give the Giants added infield depth, but won't supply the offence generated by Williams. Both began the season with the Mets but helped Cleveland win its second consecutive American League Central Division title.
The 28-year-old Vizcaino hit .297 with eight triples and 45 RBI for the Mets and Indians last season. He spent three years with the Chicago Cubs and joined the Mets in 1994.

"Vizcaino provides us great versatility and leadership in our infield," Sabean said. "Jose is a legitimate switch-hitting middle infielder who can hit at the top of our order. He has become an accomplished hitter as well as an excellent defensive player."

Kent, also 28, hit a combined .278 with 12 homers and 55 RBI in 1996. He started his career with the Toronto Blue Jays and was traded to the Mets in 1992. He had 20-homer seasons in 1993 and 1995. Kent can play third base, but is more comfortable at second base.
"In Kent, we have acquired a rare commodity -- a power-hitting middle infielder," Sabean said.
